skill.name: distributed-tracing
skill.description: Implement distributed tracing with Jaeger, Tempo, and OpenTelemetry for request flow visibility across microservices.
skill.summary: Guides distributed tracing setup, instrumentation, sampling, and troubleshooting for microservice systems.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline file references, and language examples rather than executable skill code. The Kubernetes setup example does include a remote manifest application flow, which should require review and explicit approval before use. I also found a low-severity privacy concern around recommending user_id trace tags without minimization guidance.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running kubectl commands, pin the Jaeger Operator version, and instruct users to inspect or verify remote manifests before applying them.

remediation.issue: Trace attributes may contain personal data
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to avoid raw user identifiers in spans. Prefer pseudonymous IDs, allowlists for attributes, retention limits, and restricted access to tracing backends.

remediation.issue: Example endpoints and images need production hardening
remediation.suggestion: Label placeholders as examples and advise users to replace latest tags, internal URLs, storage settings, and access controls with environment-specific values.

content.value_statement: Microservice teams need clear request paths across services. This skill guides Jaeger, Tempo, OpenTelemetry instrumentation, sampling, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Explains traces, spans, context, tags, and logs.
Shows Jaeger setup examples for Kubernetes and Docker Compose.
Provides OpenTelemetry instrumentation patterns for Python, Node.js, and Go.
Demonstrates HTTP trace context propagation across services.
Covers Tempo configuration, sampling strategies, trace queries, and correlated logs.
limitations: Example endpoints and service names must be replaced.
Does not provision credentials, storage policies, or access controls.
Does not verify compatibility with every OpenTelemetry version.

use_cases.title: Debug Slow Requests
use_cases.description: Map a request across frontend, gateway, service, and database spans to find latency sources.

use_cases.title: Plan Tracing Rollout
use_cases.description: Choose Jaeger or Tempo setup patterns, sampling rates, and instrumentation points for a service platform.

use_cases.title: Improve Incident Analysis
use_cases.description: Correlate traces, errors, and logs so incident teams can follow failure propagation across services.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Trace Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how traces, spans, context propagation, tags, and logs work in a microservice request path.

prompt_templates.title: Design A Tracing Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a distributed tracing plan for these services: [services]. Include span names, key attributes, and propagation boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Jaeger Or Tempo
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a Jaeger or Tempo setup for [environment]. Include storage, collectors, sampling, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Trace Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze why traces are missing between [service A] and [service B]. Check propagation, exporters, sampling, network paths, and logs.

output_examples.input: Trace a slow checkout request across five services.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step tracing plan with service spans, latency attributes, sampling guidance, and Jaeger queries for slow operations.

output_examples.input: Prepare tracing for a new payments service.
output_examples.output: An instrumentation checklist covering service names, span boundaries, error recording, context propagation, and production validation.
A troubleshooting path that checks collector endpoints, exporter configuration, sampling settings, network reachability, and application logs.

best_practices: Start with critical request paths before instrumenting every operation.
Use consistent service names, span names, and approved attributes.
Validate sampling, exporter health, and trace visibility in each environment.
anti_patterns: Adding high-cardinality or personal data to spans without controls.
Copying example endpoints or storage settings directly into production.
Running cluster setup commands without reviewing manifests and permissions.

faq.question: What tracing tools does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Jaeger, Grafana Tempo, and OpenTelemetry instrumentation patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with Python, Node.js, and Go services?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for Flask, Express, and Go OpenTelemetry tracing.

faq.question: Does it deploy tracing infrastructure automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides setup guidance that must be reviewed before commands are run.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production systems?
faq.answer: Yes, after adapting storage, sampling, security, retention, and access controls to the environment.

faq.question: Can it troubleshoot missing traces?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests checks for collector endpoints, network connectivity, sampling, exporters, and application logs.

faq.question: How should sensitive data be handled?
faq.answer: Avoid raw personal data in spans. Use approved attributes, pseudonymous identifiers, and restricted trace access.
